failures.triage_note: A subscriber-role member (submitter, and by the same mechanism reviewer/claimer/credituser/qa_vendor_01 — every persona this runbook labels 'subscribers') cannot upload the REQUIRED Featured Image in the submission wizard on any site running WooCommerce with default settings, which blocks the wizard from ever completing for that role. Root-caused, not guessed: reproduced twice (two different PNGs) as `submitter`, ruled out as a submitter-specific fluke by reproducing the SAME 302 via raw curl, then ruled out as a Listora capability gap (submitter has upload_files=true, granted by Listora itself) by tracing the redirect target `http://listora.local/my-account/` to WooCommerce's own `WC_Admin::prevent_admin_access()` (wp-content/plugins/woocommerce/includes/admin/class-wc-admin.php:176-214, hooked on admin_init since WC 3.6.0): it 302-redirects ANY request under /wp-admin/*.php to My Account for a user lacking edit_posts/manage_woocommerce/view_admin_dashboard, and its own exemption list only covers admin-post.php and admin-ajax.php — NOT async-upload.php, which is exactly what wp.media's classic uploader POSTs to. Confirmed the cutoff is precisely at edit_posts by testing contributor1 (has edit_posts natively) — upload succeeded immediately, and I completed the full 6-step wizard end-to-end as contributor1 with that image. The wizard's own error message ('An error occurred in the upload. Please try again later.') gives the member zero indication of the real cause.
failures.expected: A subscriber/customer-role member can upload a Featured Image via the submission wizard's media picker on a WooCommerce-active site (WooCommerce is Listora's own documented monetization backend — Credits tab shows a live WooCommerce product, 'Buying via Stripe / PayPal / WooCommerce flow' per E.credit-system).
failures.actual: POST to wp-admin/async-upload.php 302-redirects to /my-account/ before the file is ever processed, for any role without edit_posts/manage_woocommerce/view_admin_dashboard. The submission wizard's Media step surfaces a generic 'An error occurred in the upload. Please try again later.' and permanently blocks Continue, because Featured Image is required.
failures.steps_to_reproduce: 1. Ensure WooCommerce is active with default settings (this site: 11.0.1). 2. Log in as a subscriber/customer-role member (e.g. `?autologin=submitter`). 3. Go to /add-listing/, pick any type, fill Basic Info + Details, reach the Media step. 4. Click 'Click to upload or drag & drop' for Featured Image -> Select Files in the WP media modal -> pick any image. 5. Observe 'An error occurred in the upload. Please try again later.' — DevTools Network shows POST wp-admin/async-upload.php -> 302 -> /my-account/. Compare against a contributor+ role (has edit_posts): identical steps succeed immediately.
failures.opus_evidence: Mechanism confirmed in WooCommerce source (class-wc-admin.php:176-193; exempted_paths is exactly admin-post.php + admin-ajax.php) and reproduced with a control: submitter+WC-on -> 302 /my-account/, submitter+WC-OFF -> 403, contributor1+WC-on -> 403. Both users have upload_files: true; only edit_posts differs. SCOPE CORRECTION: the draft said the member cannot upload 'at all'. Not so — the wizard has TWO upload paths and only the wp.media picker uses async-upload.php. The drag-and-drop zone posts to /wp/v2/media, which was verified working under identical conditions (POST /wp-json/wp/v2/media as submitter with WC active -> 201 Created). So there is a working path; the picker is simply the discoverable one and its error message never mentions the alternative. That makes the fix small: point the picker at the same transport the drop zone already uses, 20 lines away in view.js:748-753.
